events.title: The first peoples in the basin of Mexico
events.description: Hunters camp beside the lakes of the central basin, leaving butchered mammoth bones at Tepexpan and Santa Isabel Iztapan.

events.title: Clovis hunters and the end of the megafauna
events.description: Fluted points appear across northern Mexico as mammoth, horse and giant sloth disappear from the record within a few centuries.

events.title: Maize domesticated in the Balsas valley
events.description: Farmers in the Balsas river valley begin selecting teosinte into maize. It becomes the staple of the whole hemisphere and the foundation of every civilisation that follows.

events.title: Squash, beans and chilli
events.description: Cave deposits at Guila Naquitz and Tehuacan show squash, beans, chilli and avocado in cultivation, completing the Mesoamerican crop package.

events.title: The first villages and pottery
events.description: Permanent farming villages appear on the Pacific coast of Chiapas and in the central highlands, with fired pottery and the first signs of rank.

events.title: San Lorenzo and the Olmec
events.description: The first Mesoamerican civilisation takes shape on the Gulf coast, with monumental earthworks, a ruling elite and long-distance trade in jade and obsidian.

events.title: The colossal heads carved
events.description: Basalt heads up to three metres high and twenty tonnes in weight are carved as portraits of rulers, and moved sixty kilometres without wheels or draught animals.

events.title: La Venta at its height
events.description: La Venta becomes the largest Olmec centre, with a great clay pyramid, buried offerings of jade figurines and the earliest ballcourts.

events.title: Rubber and the ballgame
events.description: The Mesoamerican ballgame is played with a solid rubber ball in purpose-built courts, a ritual contest that spreads to every later culture in the region.

events.title: Monte Alban founded
events.description: The Zapotecs level a mountaintop above the Oaxaca valley and build a city on it, occupied continuously for the next fourteen hundred years.

events.title: Zapotec writing
events.description: Carved slabs at Monte Alban carry named captives and dates - among the earliest writing in the Americas.

events.title: The Long Count calendar
events.description: Mesoamerican astronomers combine a 260-day ritual cycle with a solar year and an absolute day count running from a fixed point in 3114 BCE.

events.title: Teotihuacan founded
events.description: A city is laid out on a grid in the valley north-east of the lakes. Within two centuries it is one of the largest cities in the world.

events.title: The Pyramid of the Sun
events.description: Teotihuacan builds a pyramid sixty-five metres high on an avenue aligned to the mountains and the sky. Nobody knows what language its builders spoke.

events.title: Cuicuilco destroyed by lava
events.description: The eruption of Xitle buries Cuicuilco, Teotihuacan's main rival in the basin, and leaves the field to Teotihuacan.

events.title: The Maya Classic period begins
events.description: Maya city-states across the Yucatan, Peten and Chiapas begin raising dated stelae, recording dynasties, wars and alliances in a full writing system.

events.title: Teotihuacan intervenes at Tikal
events.description: A stela records the arrival of a Teotihuacan lord at Tikal and the death of its king on the same day. Central Mexican power reaches deep into the Maya world.

events.title: Teotihuacan at its height
events.description: The city holds perhaps 125,000 people in planned apartment compounds, with a distinct barrio for Oaxacan migrants and another for Gulf coast traders.

events.title: Teotihuacan burns
events.description: The ceremonial centre is deliberately burned and the sculptures smashed. The evidence points to a rising from inside rather than an invasion.

events.title: Pakal takes the throne at Palenque
events.description: K'inich Janaab Pakal accedes at twelve and reigns for sixty-eight years, rebuilding Palenque and leaving the longest inscriptions in the Maya corpus.

events.title: Pakal buried under the Temple of the Inscriptions
events.description: Pakal is laid in a carved sarcophagus in a vaulted chamber deep inside a pyramid, with a jade mask - a royal tomb of a kind nobody expected to find in the Americas.

events.title: The Bonampak murals
events.description: Painted walls at Bonampak show a battle, the torture of prisoners and a court procession in full colour, which ends the idea of the peaceful Maya.

events.title: The Classic Maya collapse
events.description: One southern city after another stops raising monuments and is abandoned. Drought, warfare, soil exhaustion and dynastic failure all appear in the record.

events.title: Monte Alban abandoned
events.description: The Zapotec capital is left, and the Oaxaca valley fragments into small competing kingdoms based in the lowlands.

events.title: Tula and the Toltecs
events.description: A militarised state at Tula dominates central Mexico. Later Aztec rulers claim descent from it and treat its art as the model of civilisation.

events.title: Chichen Itza rises
events.description: Chichen Itza becomes the dominant power in the northern Yucatan, its architecture mixing Maya and central Mexican forms, with a sacred cenote at its heart.

events.title: Tula falls
events.description: Tula is burned and abandoned, and groups speaking Nahuatl move south into the basin of Mexico over the following century.

events.title: Tenochtitlan founded
events.description: The Mexica, the last and least welcome arrivals in the basin, settle an island in Lake Texcoco - by tradition where they see an eagle on a cactus.

events.title: The first Mexica ruler
events.description: Acamapichtli is installed as tlatoani, giving the Mexica a dynasty with Toltec descent and a place in the region's politics.

events.title: The Triple Alliance
events.description: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan overthrow their Tepanec overlords and form the alliance that becomes the Aztec empire.

events.title: Moctezuma I and the imperial system
events.description: Conquest is systematised into a tribute empire: local rulers stay in place and send goods, and Tlacaelel rewrites the histories to justify it.

events.title: Four years of famine
events.description: Frost and drought bring famine to the basin. Thousands sell themselves into slavery on the Gulf coast, and the state expands to secure food supply.

events.title: The Templo Mayor rededicated
events.description: The great double pyramid is rededicated with mass human sacrifice, staged in front of invited enemy lords as an instrument of terror and diplomacy.

events.title: The chinampas feed a quarter million people
events.description: Raised beds built out into the lake produce several crops a year, supporting a city larger than any in Spain, supplied by canoe and aqueduct.

events.title: Moctezuma II succeeds
events.description: Moctezuma II centralises the empire, replaces the nobility with his own appointees, and fails to subdue the Tlaxcalans on his own doorstep.

events.title: Cortes lands on the coast
events.description: Hernan Cortes sails from Cuba against his governor's orders, founds Veracruz, scuttles his ships and marches inland with about five hundred men.

events.title: The Tlaxcalan alliance
events.description: After heavy fighting, Tlaxcala allies with Cortes against the Aztecs. Tens of thousands of indigenous troops do most of the fighting in the war that follows.

events.title: Cortes enters Tenochtitlan
events.description: Moctezuma receives the Spanish on the causeway and lodges them in the palace. Within a week he is effectively their prisoner.

events.title: The Toxcatl massacre
events.description: Spanish troops kill celebrants at a festival in the sacred precinct while Cortes is away. The city rises and Moctezuma dies in the fighting.

events.title: La Noche Triste
events.description: The Spanish are driven off the causeways at night with heavy losses. Cortes retreats to Tlaxcala and starts again with allies and a siege plan.

events.title: Smallpox reaches the basin
events.description: Smallpox arrives with the Spanish and kills perhaps a third of the population of central Mexico in a year, including Moctezuma's successor.

events.title: Tenochtitlan falls
events.description: After a ninety-three-day siege that cuts the aqueduct and destroys the city block by block, Cuauhtemoc surrenders. The Aztec empire ends.

events.title: Mexico City built on the ruins
events.description: The Spanish lay out a new capital on the same island, using the temple stone for the cathedral and keeping the causeways and the aqueducts.

events.title: The twelve Franciscans arrive
events.description: Twelve friars walk from Veracruz to Mexico City and begin a mass conversion campaign, learning Nahuatl and destroying temples in about equal measure.

events.title: The apparition of Guadalupe
events.description: An indigenous man named Juan Diego reports a vision of the Virgin at Tepeyac. The cult becomes the central religious fact of Mexican life.

events.title: The Viceroyalty of New Spain
events.description: Antonio de Mendoza arrives as first viceroy. New Spain becomes the wealthiest and most populous part of the Spanish empire.

events.title: The first printing press in the Americas
events.description: A press is set up in Mexico City, printing catechisms in Nahuatl and Spanish decades before any press operates in English America.

events.title: The great cocoliztli
events.description: An epidemic, probably an indigenous haemorrhagic fever aggravated by drought, kills perhaps 80 per cent of the remaining indigenous population.

events.title: Silver found at Zacatecas
events.description: Strikes at Zacatecas and Guanajuato make New Spain the largest silver producer in the world, and the Spanish peso the first global currency.

events.title: The Chichimeca War
events.description: Forty years of war against the nomadic peoples of the northern deserts, fought over the silver road and ended by negotiation rather than conquest.

events.title: The Manila galleon
events.description: A route is opened from Acapulco to Manila. Chinese silk and porcelain come east and Mexican silver goes west, for two and a half centuries.

events.title: The Inquisition established
events.description: A tribunal is set up in Mexico City with jurisdiction over Spaniards and mixed-race colonists, though indigenous people are exempted from it.

events.title: The population collapse
events.description: Central Mexico's indigenous population has fallen from perhaps 20 million to about a million, the steepest demographic collapse in recorded history.

events.title: The draining of the lakes begins
events.description: The Desague project starts cutting a channel to drain the basin. It runs for three centuries, employs forced indigenous labour and eventually destroys the lake system.

events.title: Mexico City under water for five years
events.description: A flood leaves the city submerged for half a decade and drives out much of the population, which does not stop the drainage works being mismanaged further.

events.title: Sor Juana Ines de la Cruz born
events.description: A self-taught nun becomes the greatest poet of the Spanish Baroque in the Americas, and is silenced by the church for defending a woman's right to study.

events.title: The maize riot
events.description: Crop failure and hoarding bring a crowd that burns the viceregal palace and the city hall. It is the most serious colonial rising in the capital.

events.title: The last Maya kingdom falls
events.description: Spanish forces take Nojpeten, the Itza capital on a lake in the Peten, a hundred and seventy-six years after Tenochtitlan.

events.title: The casta system
events.description: Colonial society is sorted by descent into an elaborate hierarchy of castas, painted in series of pictures and used to allocate taxes, offices and marriage.

events.title: The Jesuits expelled
events.description: The crown expels the Jesuits from all its territories, closing colleges and missions and removing the intellectual class most identified with the American-born elite.

events.title: The Bourbon reforms and free trade
events.description: Madrid opens colonial ports to wider trade and tightens tax collection, raising revenue while pushing the creole elite towards resentment.

events.title: Humboldt's expedition
events.description: Alexander von Humboldt spends a year in New Spain and publishes an account of its economy and geography that Europe reads as a description of untapped wealth.

events.title: The Consolidation decree
events.description: The crown demands that church mortgages be called in to fund its wars. Credit dries up across New Spain and much of the elite is ruined.

events.title: Napoleon takes Spain
events.description: With the Spanish king deposed, the question of who is legitimately sovereign in New Spain becomes open. A creole attempt at self-government is put down by a coup.

events.title: The Grito de Dolores
events.description: A parish priest, Miguel Hidalgo, calls his congregation to rise. The date becomes Mexican independence day, though he is dead within a year.

events.title: Hidalgo executed
events.description: Hidalgo is caught, defrocked and shot, and his head is displayed in Guanajuato for a decade. The rising fragments into guerrilla war.

events.title: Morelos and the Congress of Chilpancingo
events.description: Jose Maria Morelos convenes a congress that declares independence, abolishes slavery and the caste system, and drafts a constitution.

events.title: Morelos executed
events.description: The insurgency's best commander is captured and shot. Resistance is reduced to a few bands in the mountains for five years.

events.title: Independence
events.description: Agustin de Iturbide, a royalist commander, changes sides, allies with the insurgent Guerrero and negotiates independence under the Plan of Iguala.

events.title: Iturbide crowned emperor
events.description: Iturbide has himself made emperor and lasts ten months. Central America leaves, and Mexico's first experiment in government ends in a coup.

events.title: The federal constitution
events.description: A federal republic is established on a broadly American model, with strong states and a weak centre. The argument between federalists and centralists dominates the next fifty years.

events.title: Slavery abolished
events.description: Vicente Guerrero, himself of African and indigenous descent, abolishes slavery, thirty-six years before the United States.

events.title: Santa Anna's first presidency
events.description: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna takes the presidency for the first of eleven times, and abolishes the federal constitution two years later.

events.title: Texas secedes
events.description: Anglo settlers and Tejanos declare independence, lose the Alamo and win at San Jacinto, capturing Santa Anna. Mexico refuses to recognise the result.

events.title: The Pastry War
events.description: France blockades Veracruz over unpaid claims including a looted pastry shop. Santa Anna loses a leg and buries it with military honours.

events.title: The war with the United States
events.description: The annexation of Texas leads to invasion. American armies take Veracruz, Monterrey and finally Mexico City after the fighting at Chapultepec.

events.title: The Caste War of Yucatan begins
events.description: Maya communities rise against the Yucatecan elite and hold much of the peninsula for decades. The last rebel territory is not taken until 1901.

events.title: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
events.description: Mexico cedes about half its territory - California, Nevada, Utah, most of Arizona and New Mexico - for fifteen million dollars.

events.title: The Gadsden Purchase
events.description: Santa Anna sells a further strip of northern desert to the United States, which finishes the modern border and finishes him politically.

events.title: The Revolution of Ayutla and La Reforma
events.description: A liberal rising drives out Santa Anna for good and brings in a generation - Juarez, Ocampo, Lerdo - committed to breaking the power of the church and the army.

events.title: The liberal constitution
events.description: A new constitution guarantees civil liberties, strips the church of its lands and abolishes special courts. The conservatives take up arms against it.

events.title: The War of the Reform
events.description: Three years of civil war between liberals and conservatives end with Juarez entering Mexico City and the church's estates nationalised.

events.title: Juarez suspends the debt
events.description: Bankrupted by the civil war, Juarez suspends payments to foreign creditors. Britain, Spain and France send fleets to Veracruz.

events.title: The Battle of Puebla
events.description: A smaller Mexican force defeats the French army at Puebla. It delays the invasion by a year and is still celebrated as Cinco de Mayo.

events.title: Maximilian crowned emperor
events.description: With French bayonets and conservative support, an Austrian archduke is installed as Emperor of Mexico. Juarez governs from a carriage in the north.

events.title: Maximilian executed and the republic restored
events.description: With French troops withdrawn, Maximilian is captured at Queretaro and shot. Juarez returns to Mexico City and the conservative party is finished.

events.title: Juarez dies in office
events.description: Juarez dies of a heart attack having held the state together through invasion and civil war. Within four years the army takes over again.

events.title: Porfirio Diaz takes power
events.description: Diaz seizes the presidency on a platform of no re-election, and then governs for thirty-four years under the slogan order and progress.

events.title: The railway boom
events.description: Foreign capital builds twenty thousand kilometres of track, tying the mines and haciendas to the American border and the ports.

events.title: The land law
events.description: A survey law lets companies claim untitled land. Village commons are taken wholesale, and by 1910 a small number of families hold most of the countryside.

events.title: Regeneracion and the Flores Magon brothers
events.description: An opposition newspaper begins publishing and is repeatedly shut down. Its editors move to the United States and turn to anarchism.

events.title: The Cananea strike
events.description: Copper miners strike against a two-tier wage system for Mexican and American workers. Arizona Rangers cross the border to help put it down.

events.title: Rio Blanco
events.description: Textile workers at Rio Blanco are fired on by the army. Between fifty and several hundred are killed, and the regime's labour settlement collapses.

events.title: The Creelman interview
events.description: Diaz tells an American journalist that Mexico is ready for democracy and he will not stand again. The opposition takes him at his word and organises.

events.title: The centenary celebrations
events.description: Diaz spends lavishly on the independence centenary while the election that returns him for an eighth term is openly rigged and his opponent imprisoned.

events.title: The Revolution begins
events.description: Francisco Madero, escaped to Texas, calls for a rising. Risings start in Chihuahua under Pascual Orozco and Pancho Villa, and in Morelos under Zapata.

events.title: Diaz resigns
events.description: After the fall of Ciudad Juarez, Diaz resigns and sails for Paris. Madero is elected president in the freest election Mexico has yet held.

events.title: The Plan de Ayala
events.description: Zapata breaks with Madero over land reform and issues the Plan de Ayala, demanding the return of village lands. Land and liberty becomes the slogan.

events.title: The Ten Tragic Days
events.description: A coup in Mexico City backed by the American ambassador ends with Madero and his vice-president murdered and Victoriano Huerta in power.

events.title: The Constitutionalists take the field
events.description: Carranza, Obregon, Villa and Zapata make war on Huerta from four directions, in what becomes the bloodiest phase of the revolution.

events.title: The United States occupies Veracruz
events.description: American marines seize Veracruz over a diplomatic insult, cutting Huerta's arms supply and hardening Mexican nationalism for a generation.

events.title: The Convention of Aguascalientes
events.description: The victorious factions meet to agree a government and fail. Villa and Zapata ride into Mexico City together, and the war restarts among the winners.

events.title: Celaya
events.description: Obregon, using trenches, machine guns and barbed wire learned from Europe, destroys Villa's cavalry at Celaya. The northern division never recovers.

events.title: Villa raids Columbus
events.description: Villa attacks a town in New Mexico and Pershing pursues him into Mexico for eleven months without catching him.

events.title: The Constitution of 1917
events.description: The new constitution puts subsoil rights in the nation, guarantees the eight-hour day and the right to strike, and provides for land redistribution. It is still in force.

events.title: Zapata assassinated
events.description: Zapata is lured into an ambush and shot. The land reform he fought for is written into law and delivered slowly, for decades, by his enemies' party.

events.title: Carranza killed and Obregon takes over
events.description: Carranza is killed fleeing a rising by his own generals. Obregon takes the presidency, and the revolution settles into a government.

events.title: The muralists commissioned
events.description: Vasconcelos puts Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros to work painting public buildings, creating the visual language in which Mexico tells its own history.

events.title: Villa assassinated
events.description: Villa is shot in his car in Parral three years after retiring to a hacienda. Every major revolutionary leader is now dead by violence.

events.title: The Cristero War
events.description: Enforcement of the constitution's anticlerical articles provokes a Catholic rising in the west. Perhaps ninety thousand die before a negotiated settlement.

events.title: The party of the revolution founded
events.description: After Obregon's assassination, Calles founds a single party to manage succession without bloodshed. Renamed the PRI, it holds power for seventy-one years.

events.title: Cardenas and the land reform
events.description: Lazaro Cardenas distributes some eighteen million hectares to village ejidos, organises labour into the party, and takes in refugees from the Spanish war.

events.title: The oil expropriation
events.description: Cardenas nationalises the foreign oil companies after they defy a labour ruling. Ordinary Mexicans queue to donate to the compensation fund, and PEMEX is founded.

events.title: The Bracero Program
events.description: Mexico enters the war on the Allied side and agrees to supply contract farm labour to the United States. Four and a half million contracts are issued over twenty-two years.

events.title: The Mexican miracle
events.description: Import substitution and public investment give twenty-five years of growth above six per cent a year, and move the country from rural to urban.

events.title: Women get the vote
events.description: Women win the right to vote in federal elections, twenty-four years after the first state granted it and eight years after the war that changed everything else.

events.title: The Tlatelolco massacre
events.description: Ten days before the Olympics open in Mexico City, soldiers fire on a student demonstration at Tlatelolco. The death toll is still disputed and the regime's legitimacy never recovers.

events.title: The oil boom
events.description: Huge Gulf discoveries and high prices fund a spending spree financed by foreign debt, on the assumption that oil will stay expensive.

events.title: The debt crisis
events.description: Mexico announces it cannot service its debt. The peso collapses, the banks are nationalised, and the Latin American debt crisis begins here.

events.title: The Mexico City earthquake
events.description: An earthquake kills at least ten thousand people. The government's paralysis and the self-organised rescue effort mark the start of independent civil society.

events.title: The stolen election
events.description: The vote count collapses and Carlos Salinas is declared winner over Cuauhtemoc Cardenas. The ballots are later burned by act of congress.

events.title: The ejido reform
events.description: The constitution is amended to allow communal village land to be sold, reversing the central social achievement of the revolution.

events.title: NAFTA and the Zapatista rising
events.description: On the day the trade agreement takes effect, an indigenous army occupies towns in Chiapas. Mexico's two futures are announced within hours of each other.

events.title: Colosio assassinated
events.description: The governing party's presidential candidate is shot at a rally in Tijuana. The killing is never satisfactorily explained.

events.title: The peso crisis
events.description: A botched devaluation triggers capital flight and a fifty billion dollar American rescue. Output falls by six per cent in a year.

events.title: The PRI loses power
events.description: Vicente Fox wins the presidency and ends seventy-one years of single-party rule, in what is generally taken as the completion of the transition to democracy.

events.title: The drug war declared
events.description: Felipe Calderon sends the army against the cartels after winning by half a percentage point. The homicide rate triples over the following decade.

events.title: The forty-three of Ayotzinapa
events.description: Forty-three student teachers are taken by police in Iguala and never found. The case comes to stand for the collapse of the line between the state and organised crime.

events.title: Lopez Obrador wins
events.description: Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador wins the presidency with the largest margin in modern Mexican history, on his third attempt, and breaks the two-party system.

events.title: The pandemic
events.description: Mexico records one of the world's highest excess death tolls relative to population, and the informal economy has no cushion.

events.title: Nearshoring makes Mexico America's largest trading partner
events.description: Supply chains moving out of China make Mexico the United States' biggest trade partner, and the northern industrial cities boom again.

events.title: Claudia Sheinbaum elected
events.description: Mexico elects its first woman president, a climate scientist, with about sixty per cent of the vote.
